import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

def get_left (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ l _ => some l
  | _ => none

def get_right (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ r => some r
  | _ => none

def get_val (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v _ _ => some v
  | _ => none

def BinarySearchTree.is_node (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ _ => True
  | _ => False

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zig_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t ∧ 
  BinarySearchTree.is_node t ∧ 
  (match get_left t with | some l => BinarySearchTree.is_node l | none => False)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def zig (t : BinarySearchTree) 
    (h_precond : zig_precond t) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node y (BinarySearchTree.Node x a b) c =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node x a (BinarySearchTree.Node y b c)
  | other => other
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zig_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : zig_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t ∧
  -- Structural properties
  get_val result = get_val (get_left t).get! ∧
  BinarySearchTree.is_node (get_right result).get! ∧
  get_val (get_right result).get! = get_val t
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma zig_rotate_view (x y : Int) (a b c : BinarySearchTree) :
    view (BinarySearchTree.Node x a (BinarySearchTree.Node y b c)) =
      view (BinarySearchTree.Node y (BinarySearchTree.Node x a b) c) := by
  ext z
  simp [view]
  tauto

lemma zig_rotate_bst (x y : Int) (a b c : BinarySearchTree)
    (h : is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node y (BinarySearchTree.Node x a b) c)) :
    is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node x a (BinarySearchTree.Node y b c)) := by
  dsimp [is_bst] at h ⊢
  rcases h with ⟨hLeftLessY, hLeftBST, hRightGreaterY, hRightBST⟩
  rcases hLeftBST with ⟨hALessX, hABST, hBGreaterX, hBBST⟩
  have hXY : x < y := by
    exact hLeftLessY x (by simp [view])
  refine ⟨hALessX, hABST, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro z hz
    have hz' : z = y ∨ z ∈ view b ∨ z ∈ view c := by
      simpa [view] using hz
    rcases hz' with hzY | hzB | hzC
    · simpa [hzY] using hXY
    · exact hBGreaterX z hzB
    · exact lt_trans hXY (hRightGreaterY z hzC)
  · refine ⟨?_, hBBST, hRightGreaterY, hRightBST⟩
    intro z hzB
    exact hLeftLessY z (by simp [view, hzB])
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem zig_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree)
    (h_precond : zig_precond t) :
    zig_postcond t (zig t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  cases t with
  | Empty =>
      have hfalse : False := by
        simpa [zig_precond, BinarySearchTree.is_node] using h_precond.2.1
      exact False.elim hfalse
  | Node y l c =>
      cases l with
      | Empty =>
          have hfalse : False := by
            simpa [get_left, BinarySearchTree.is_node] using h_precond.2.2
          exact False.elim hfalse
      | Node x a b =>
          have hbst :
              is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node y (BinarySearchTree.Node x a b) c) :=
            h_precond.1
          simp [zig_postcond, zig, get_left, get_right, get_val,
            BinarySearchTree.is_node]
          exact ⟨zig_rotate_bst x y a b c hbst, zig_rotate_view x y a b c⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

analysis:
The student’s submission does implement the required Zig operation as a single right rotation on a BST node with a non-empty left child.

What the problem requires:
1. Implement a BST and preserve the BST invariant.
2. Focus on Zig (single right rotation).
3. Prove:
   - the mathematical set of values (`view`) is unchanged,
   - the BST invariant is preserved,
   - the structural correctness: original left child becomes new root, original root becomes new right child.
4. No cheating tricks such as `sorry`, `admit`, empty body, or outsourcing the real work to existing verified functions.

What the student implemented:
- A custom inductive tree type `BinarySearchTree` with constructors `Empty` and `Node`.
- A set-valued `view`.
- A BST invariant `is_bst`.
- A `zig` function:
  ```lean
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node y (BinarySearchTree.Node x a b) c =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node x a (BinarySearchTree.Node y b c)
  | other => other
  ```
  This is exactly the standard single right rotation (zig).
- Supporting lemmas:
  - `zig_rotate_view`: proves set preservation.
  - `zig_rotate_bst`: proves BST invariant preservation.
- Final theorem `zig_postcond_satisfied` proving the postcondition under the precondition.

Structural correctness:
- After rotation, the new root is the original left child’s value `x`.
- The new right child is `Node y b c`, so the original root becomes the new right child.
This matches the natural language requirement.

Cheating check:
- No `sorry`, `admit`, placeholders, or empty implementation.
- No use of built-in BST rotation/set libraries to avoid doing the work.
- The rotation is implemented directly from scratch.
- The proof is also written explicitly.

Minor note:
- The structural postcondition checks root/new-right-child values and node-ness, not every subtree relation in maximal detail, but the actual implementation itself is the correct zig rotation, so semantically it matches the required algorithm.
